title: Durga in the Sky: The Constellations Behind the Goddess
description:
Durga Puja and Navaratri are celebrated with grandeur across India, but what if the story of Goddess Durga and Mahishasura actually began in the night sky? In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we trace the origins of the Durga vs Mahishasura legend to the constellations Virgo, Leo, Orion, and Taurus. The image of Durga riding a lion, slaying the bull-headed demon Mahishasura, mirrors how ancient cultures connected stars to stories.

We explore how Virgo (the virgin woman), Leo (the lion), Orion (the hunter), and Taurus (the bull) shaped the mythology of Durga, and how similar sky stories existed in Mesopotamia, Greece, Egypt, and even in Norse mythology. The video also reveals a surprising parallel: the same star patterns that inspired Durga’s myth also map onto the Adam and Eve story, complete with the serpent Hydra, a woman (Virgo), a man (Bootes), and the forbidden fruit.

This isn’t just about religion—it’s about how humans used the sky as a calendar, a GPS, and a storytelling canvas. These myths were once tools to track time and seasons, but over centuries, they became religious narratives. By revisiting the science of constellations, we can see how stories of Durga Puja, Vijayadashami, Dussehra, and Navratri are part of a global pattern of sky-based myths.

#DurgaPuja #Navratri #MythologyExplained #palebluethoughts 

00:00 – Intro: Myth Meets Astronomy
01:10 – Mapping Durga: Virgo, Leo, Orion, Taurus
03:20 – Global Parallels in Star Myths
05:10 – Sky as Calendar & Navigation
06:40 – Adam–Eve Parallels in Constellations
08:00 – Why These Stories Persist
09:10 – Conclusion
